items.streamTitle: Cross-cultural norm strength depended on the specific norm being measured
items.streamSummary: Two studies (N=3,344) across Japan, South Korea, the US and UK found norm-strength comparisons changed with referent, type, context, measure and valence; within-region differences often exceeded between-region differences. No uniform cultural ranking was supported.
items.attribution: Vishkin, Kaspi, Miyamoto et al. — Communications Psychology (two cross-national studies; November 21, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Policy uncertainty correlated with a gap between AI strategy announcements and staffing
items.streamSummary: An observational study of Chinese listed firms (2016–2024) linked economic policy uncertainty to a wider AI-strategy-versus-staffing gap and weaker later firm outcomes. Disclosures and hiring are proxies, not direct evidence of strategic intent or causality.
items.attribution: Zhang, Cao, Cao and Yao — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (firm panel study; November 21, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Taiwan flagged suspected election-influence networks; Meta disputed their electoral activity
items.streamSummary: Taiwan said it referred nearly 2,700 suspected accounts and a separate AI-video network to Meta before local elections. Meta disputed election posting among flagged accounts. Attribution, exposure and effects on voters are unresolved.
items.attribution: Yimou Lee / Reuters — reporting from Taiwanese officials, internal reports and Meta response (November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Scale-consistent community memberships revealed hidden diversity in aggregated networks
items.streamSummary: LFMM preserved mixed community membership across geographic aggregation scales in a large Dutch social network and exposed diverse urban ties hidden by single-community assignments. It measures structure, not influence outcomes.
items.attribution: Adel, Bokányi, Heemskerk and Takes — npj Complexity (network-methods paper; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Meaning-making correlated with proactive service under emotional demands
items.streamSummary: Two-wave data from 470 Chinese community workers associated emotional job demands with proactive service via modeled meaning-making, particularly among future-oriented workers. The study is observational, not a causal test of meaning-making training.
items.attribution: Zhan, Gan, Yue et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (two-wave organizational survey; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Agents building other agents failed to generalize beyond their self-made tests
items.streamSummary: AppSci-Bench evaluated seven models building agents for seven applied workflows; the best achieved a 59.1% mean-minimum score across three attempts, and self-built tests often failed to predict held-out success. These are simulated workflow results.
items.attribution: Srivastava, Kaur, Chang et al. — arXiv AppSci-Bench preprint (November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Compressing an AI agent's history sometimes turned unresolved work into false conclusions
items.streamSummary: CompAct-Bench resumed agents after compressing successful research, coding and workplace trajectories; aggressive compaction reduced completion and sometimes rewrote unresolved issues as conclusions. Results are benchmark-specific.
items.attribution: Chen, Chen, Chen et al. — arXiv CompAct-Bench preprint (November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Open longitudinal party-position panel integrates text and expert judgments with uncertainty
items.streamSummary: A November 21 Scientific Data release provides Bayesian economic/cultural position estimates for 708 parties in 65 countries across 1944–2025, integrating text and experts with uncertainty. It is contextual data infrastructure, not voter-level measurement.
items.attribution: Armin Seimel — Scientific Data (cross-national party-position dataset descriptor; November 21, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Friendship-based chatbot intervention improved relational outcomes but not overall wellbeing
items.streamSummary: A preregistered cluster RCT (251 young adults) found a six-week chatbot program for existing friendship groups improved perceived friend support and selected PERMA dimensions, but not overall wellbeing or loneliness.
items.attribution: Turóczi, Szabó, Verebélyi et al. — Scientific Reports (preregistered cluster randomized trial; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Facial self-resemblance did not reliably make conversational partners more likable
items.streamSummary: A preregistered 60-person, yoked-video experiment found no general liking benefit from self-resembling faces. Exploratory self-esteem differences suggest heterogeneity, not a confirmed universal social-bonding mechanism.
items.attribution: Kasahara, Claggett and Shirado — Scientific Reports (preregistered online social-perception experiment; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: AI use and academic procrastination were associated through anxiety and self-control
items.streamSummary: A cross-sectional survey of 782 Chinese university students linked AI use with procrastination and modeled indirect associations through anxiety and self-control; simultaneous self-reports prohibit causal conclusions.
items.attribution: Wu and Zhou — Scientific Reports (cross-sectional university survey; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Cross-post event linking improved causal-relation classification in fragmented social reports
items.streamSummary: STAGE combined weak cross-tweet supervision and spatiotemporal graphs, improving event-relation classification on wildfire and hurricane tweets, with asymmetric transfer. It detects reported causal links, not intervention causality.
items.attribution: Duong, Gary, Levin and Nguyen — arXiv preprint (cross-tweet event-relation benchmark; November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Belief–opinion coupling changed modeled echo-chamber formation
items.streamSummary: A November 19 preprint found opinion–belief coherence created more but smaller simulated belief echo chambers under specified tolerance and updating rules. It is a model result, not observed social polarization.
items.attribution: Kataoka, Euzenat and Hasebe — arXiv preprint (formal opinion/belief simulation; November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: UNESCO–UCL found AI systems vulnerable to user pushback and multilingual reasoning gaps
items.streamSummary: UNESCO–UCL tests of up to 33 models found frequent agreement with incorrect user challenges, uneven accuracy across 13 languages and near-chance policy-interaction judgments. These are climate-domain AI benchmarks, not observed human belief effects.
items.attribution: UNESCO and University College London — Can We Trust AI on Climate? (original report; UNESCO release November 16, updated November 18, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Baltic information-war review traced identity grievances across organizations and media channels
items.streamSummary: An October 28 FPRI report traces Russian information activity in the Baltic states through historical-memory disputes, identity narratives and state-linked organizations. It offers a strategic case framework, not causal persuasion estimates.
items.attribution: Briana List, Robert Person and Reagan Phelps — Foreign Policy Research Institute (historical strategic report; October 28, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Geotagged citizen perceptions linked lived experience to observable environmental choices
items.streamSummary: A Japanese citizen-science platform linked 8,225 location-tagged perception reports from 648 people to visual features and pilot behavior observations. Pre–post gains after design changes are not causal proof; the contribution is a context-rich measurement workflow.
items.attribution: Nishii, Sato, Kataoka et al. — Scientific Reports (citizen-sourced smartphone perception mapping and pilots; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Phishing-link interactions varied sharply by organizational role in a real university setting
items.streamSummary: A 600-person university field study found simulated-phishing link interactions of 93.5% among administrators, 44.0% among academics and 22.5% among students. Different messages by role prevent attributing the differences to role alone.
items.attribution: Jasinska and Jasinski — Scientific Reports (observational simulated-phishing field study; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Human experts and AI judges disagreed on which drafted messages were better
items.streamSummary: In a 158-inquiry retrospective comparison, clinician graders preferred human-written messages on correctness, completeness and clarity; LLM graders favored AI drafts and agreed poorly with each other. The transferable advance is expert-calibrated evaluation, not a clinical effectiveness claim.
items.attribution: Hao, Holmes, Hobson et al. — Scientific Reports (iterative expert evaluation of AI-drafted messages; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Realistic socio-legal scenarios exposed uneven AI safeguards and identity-cue effects
items.streamSummary: A peer-reviewed benchmark of ten LLMs across 269 illicit scenarios and 50 intents found substantial failures to avoid facilitation and recognize legal risk, varying by jurisdiction, scenario and synthetic identity cues. No real-world crime outcomes were measured.
items.attribution: Wang, Xie, Wang et al. — Nature Communications (cross-jurisdiction LLM safety benchmarking; November 20, 2026)

items.streamTitle: A critical review mapped how plausible AI-agent behavior can distort collective simulation outputs
items.streamSummary: A November 17 critical review synthesized 74 contemporary generative-social-simulation studies, highlighting how micro-level bias, persona convergence and interaction rules may yield artificial macro outcomes. Its validation framework is conceptual rather than a new predictive test.
items.attribution: Taillandier, Zucker, Grignard et al. — Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence (critical review of generative social simulations; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: An online backlash grew in volume while first-person consumer criticism declined
items.streamSummary: Graphika's November case analysis found shopper/creator negative posts fell about 61% after a refund announcement even as media-driven discussion rose. Message volume alone mischaracterized the narrative trajectory; refund causality and restored trust were not established.
items.attribution: Alexandra Matheny — Graphika (original strategic-communications narrative analysis; November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Network effect decomposition separated own treatment from neighborhood exposure in simulations
items.streamSummary: NEDNet decomposed observational network outcomes into baseline, own-treatment and peer-exposure pathways, improving estimation error on semi-synthetic social-network benchmarks. Its additive interaction restriction and causal assumptions require scrutiny in field applications.
items.attribution: Huang, Zhang, Lu et al. — arXiv preprint, Network Effect Decomposition Network (causal-estimation methods; November 5, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Language comprehension related differently to children's theory of mind and empathy
items.streamSummary: Among 83 children aged 6–14, deaf and hearing groups differed on language comprehension, theory of mind and symbolic emotion recognition, but not total empathy or contextual emotion recognition. Observational mediation does not establish causality.
items.attribution: Mejía, Cardona and Baez — Scientific Reports (comparative child social-cognition study; November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Human numerosity signals emerged before non-numeric visual features
items.streamSummary: Time-resolved MEG and fMRI analyses found rapid numerosity signals preceding some non-numeric image-feature coding, with representations evolving from broad quantity to tuned number responses. Neural representational evidence does not imply numeric framing changes real-world decisions.
items.attribution: Karami, Castaldi, Eger, Hebart and Piazza — Nature Communications (MEG/fMRI representational study; November 19, 2026)
